hook: Wind up a bucket from a well and your arm makes big slow circles while the bucket creeps up. Turning a crank is doing work, just as lifting the bucket directly would be. In rotation, work is torque times angle, and it lands exactly where energy bookkeeping says it should.

ideas: W = τΔθ for a constant torque, with Δθ in radians: the partner of W = Fd.
For a changing torque, W is the area under the τ-θ graph.
Positive when the torque turns the object the way it is going; negative when it opposes.
The net work done on a turning object equals its change in rotational kinetic energy.
Convert revolutions to radians first: 1 rev = 2π rad.

misconception.wrong: Work done by a torque is τ times the number of revolutions (or degrees).
misconception.right: W = τΔθ only works with the angle in radians, because it comes from W = Fs with s = rθ. Four revolutions is 8π rad, about 25 rad.

summary: A torque that turns an object through an angle does work W = τΔθ (angle in radians), or the area under a torque-angle graph when the torque varies. The net work done on a turning object changes its rotational kinetic energy; a torque that opposes the turning does negative work.
